scope: Seven Robie House day views previously inspected after the geometry partition correction, plus all seven newly rendered post-polish night views. One additional flight-start night frame was inspected. This is a framing/material/lighting review, not a temporal-motion validation.
renderingDefectResolved: Initial galleries showed only grounds because the city vertex span crossed4GiB. The root geometry-partition correction restored all house geometry without modifying Robie geometry.
nightPolishResolved: Two modest west washes and strengthened south accents make the coping, brick and trailing planters readable while retaining warm windows and dark roof silhouettes. No further source changes recommended.

dayBeforeNightPolish.scope: Day images predate two small fixture boxes and night-only light strength changes; their exact original source hashes are retained.

releaseNight.scope: Post-polish night gallery rendered from the frozen release sources.

limitations: No claim of photographic equivalence or exact as-built dimensions.
Night reference is a brighter dusk photograph; full-night view is intentionally darker.
Procedural nearby facades and compact vegetation do not reproduce each real-world surface or mature tree.
Still images contain residual progressive grain; motion metrics are separately validated.

inspected.finding: Complete offset wings, low roof planes, garden walls and window bands read clearly in daylight.
West prow, deep cantilever, exterior terrace and transmitting glass have clear framing.
Roman brick courses, recessed joints, limestone bands and the visible lower recreation room form a useful material study.
The balcony has a clear visual aisle; geometric came and colored glass reveal the furnished living room.
Living room framing shows the pierced hearth, stepped oak ceiling, laylights, glazing and inglenook. Palette and ornament are interpretive.
Dining furniture, hearth opening and circulation remain readable. Furnishings are an approximation of the restored reference vocabulary.
Upper view exposes the hip roofs, belvedere, chimney and service wing. Nearby context is visibly less detailed than the house.
Accepted west lighting polish: masonry, limestone coping and trailing planters are readable. Warm glazing remains the main house accent; roof planes keep their full-night silhouettes.
Accepted west lighting polish: foreground parapet and planters now frame the deep canopy and central art glass. No camera clipping or newly obscured focal feature.
Stronger south accents improve the Roman brick and limestone study while preserving the lower-room glazing. No new framing defect.
Art-glass pattern, colored pieces, transmitting room light and the balcony aisle remain clear. Dark roof/porch surfaces retain visible progressive speckle.
Hearth opening, inglenook, glazed perimeter and integrated ceiling lighting remain readable at night. Warm ochre/oak interpretation remains brighter and more regular than some reference photos.
Dining furniture, central hearth and connected aisle remain legible under the interior practicals. Restored furnishing shapes are interpreted rather than scanned.
Night elevated view retains the stepped roof silhouette, belvedere glazing, window bands and restrained garden accents. Generic context windows remain less detailed.

additionalInspected.finding: McCormick Place flight start has clear roof/entry lighting and city context. This single frame does not validate the connecting flight or its temporal stability.
